raw_transcript:
Ok so, EE 342 lab, lab 5, the op-amp filter one. Wednesday night. I'm tired. Um.

So me and Tomas Rideau, my lab partner, we were supposed to build the second order low-pass Sallen-Key filter with a cutoff of 1 kilohertz. And we built it, mostly. The, the resistors were 10 kilohm and the caps, we used 15 nanofarad. No, sorry, 16 nanofarad, no, okay, the kit had 15, Tomas swapped in 16 because the TA said we could get closer to 1 k. Uh, so final was 16 nanofarad. Measured cutoff on the scope was 968 hertz, which, with the theoretical being, like, 995 hertz, is like a 3 percent error. Good enough I think.

The part that did not go well, the Bode plot. We were supposed to sweep from 100 hertz to 10 kilohertz and record gain at, um, at least 12 points. We got 9 points before the lab closed at 9 pm. Professor Lindqvist is strict about the closing time. So the Bode plot is incomplete, and we have to either come back during open lab on Friday or, or interpolate, which, no, we're not gonna fake data. We'll go Friday. Open lab is 1 to 4.

Also the rolloff, it should be minus 40 dB per decade for second order, and what we measured between 2 k and 10 k was about minus 34. Tomas thinks it's the op-amp, we used the LM358, and it's not great at higher frequencies. I don't know. I didn't really check the gain bandwidth, I should look at the datasheet before I write that in the report as a reason.

Ugh, also the soldering station on bench 6 is, like, not heating, we lost twenty minutes there. I told the TA, Hana Sorel, she said she'd log it.

The report is due Monday the 2nd at 11:59 pm on the course site. Uh, November 2nd. Tomas is writing the theory section, I'm doing the results and the discussion. I have not started the discussion. I did put the 9 data points into the spreadsheet though.

And there's the midterm, the EE 342 midterm is next Thursday, so I can't spend the whole weekend on this report. Okay that's it.

Oh, and I forgot, the, the pre-lab quiz. We both got 9 out of 10, I missed the one about the quality factor, Q, I said Q of 0.5 for Butterworth and it's 0.707. Which, I knew that. I knew that. Ugh. And our Q, from the measured response, Tomas estimated it at about 0.68, which is close to 0.707 but we haven't really double checked that estimate, he did it kind of fast from the peak, so I'm not putting it in the report as a result unless we redo it on Friday.

Also, um, for the report we need to include a SPICE simulation, LTspice, and compare it to the measured curve. I did the simulation already, actually, last night, it gives a cutoff of 993 hertz, so that's close to the hand calculation. I exported the plot. That part's done at least. Lastly I want to email Professor Lindqvist about whether the extra open-lab session counts as late work, because the syllabus says all data must be collected in the scheduled session. Hmm. I'll email him tomorrow morning. Haven't done that yet.
